hints.title: Subsequence Filtering Condition
hints.text: A dictionary word can be formed by deleting characters from s if and only if that word is a valid subsequence of s.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Subsequence Matching
hints.text: For each word w in the dictionary, scan s with a pointer to verify if all characters of w appear in s in order.

hints.title: Length and Lexicographical Ranking
hints.text: Track the best word found. Update if current valid word is longer, or equal in length but lexicographically smaller.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(D * N) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Generating all 2^N deletions from s takes exponential time and runs out of memory.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Testing each dictionary word against s takes O(N) per word with zero additional memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle the lexicographical tie-break without sorting the entire dictionary upfront.
